newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso firms up as long bond yields retreat.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso firms up as long bond yields retreat.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed firmer across the board on Tuesday due to U.S. long bond yields declining, traders said.

"Labor costs data released early sent U.S. long bond yields down and that took pressure off the peso," a trader said. The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 2.2 and 2.4 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8130/7.8180 and 7.8090/7.8130 per dollar.
At the close of peso trading in Mexico, yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were down to 6.89 percent from 6.95 percent on Monday.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 1.5 centavos firmer at 7.8050/7.8100 per dollar.

Dealers estimated the peso could trade at similar levels to Tuesday's on Wednesday, so long as primary interest rates did not fall more than 50 basis points at the central bank's weekly auction of government securities.
A Reuters survey of nine money market traders showed they predicted an average fall of 53 basis points for bellwether 28-day Cetes (Treasury Certificate) rates to 22.40 percent.
Banco de Mexico is due to announce primary auction results at 1930 EST/0030 GMT.
